newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM cargo signs single firm trucking deal.
newsitem.headline: KLM cargo signs single firm trucking deal.

text.p: KLM Cargo, the airfreight wing of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV has broken with convention and signed a six month deal with a Dutch trucking group to handle a very large share of the airline's European airport to airport freight transport next year.

A spokesman for KLM Cargo said the independently-owned Dutch trucking group Jan de Rijk BV has been selected as the company which will carry the lion's share of KLM's trucked airfreight. A contract is to be signed by both parties for the first six months of 1997.

In a telephone interview, the spokesman added: "We always have deals with transport companies for trucking purposes. In fact, all KLM's trucking requirements are sub-contracted. The difference with this contract is that Jan de Rijk made us a very good deal."

"It is the first time that such a contract has gone to a single company," he added declining to put a value on the contract or to specify the amount of truck movements or the total volume of freight involved.
But sources close to the airline estimate KLM Cargo spends some 75 million guilders annually on truck movements in and around Europe. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
